IBKR: the fee toll scales faster than per-account intensity

IBKR-intensity · USD · series 2026-09-17T20:06:06Z · built 2026-09-17 20:26 UTC

The short version

Interactive Brokers closed Q2’26 with 5.185 million accounts, $673M of commissions, 4.824M daily average revenue trades at $2.64 per cleared order, and $930.3B of customer equity. The toll keeps collecting — commissions are up 30.4% on a year ago — but the intensity of the toll eased: $129.80 of commissions per account, down 2.8%, and 7.23 bps of client equity for the quarter. Scale, not take-rate, carried the print. The API pillar is still unmeasured, and net interest income stays in the archive.

We hold IBKR for the fee toll, the API moat, and globality. This dig measures the first pillar — how much toll the franchise collects per account, per order, and per dollar of client equity. The API pillar remains a gap, not a chart. Everything below is nominal dollars unless a series is explicitly labeled real.

The toll: dollars up, per-account take down

Commissions printed $673M in Q2’26, up 30.4% on a year ago. Per account, the take was $129.80 — down 2.8% from $133.47 a year earlier; that CPA decline coincides with accounts growing 34.1% while commissions grew 30.4%. The franchise added accounts faster than it added toll per account. Other fees chipped in $16.78 per account ($87M across 5.185M accounts), a smaller line growing faster.

The cleanest intensity measure is the issuer's own: commission per cleared commissionable order. It printed $2.64, versus $2.65 a year earlier and $3.16 when the dense series begins in early 2023. That is a gentle glide, not a toll collapse — the take per order held in the mid-$2s while volume scaled.

Connecting the toll to the client-asset base: commissions were 7.23 bps of customer equity for the quarter — 28.9 bps on a simple annualized basis (×4, not TTM). Equity grew 40.0% year over year, faster than commissions, so the yield compressed even as commission dollars rose. Part of that equity growth is market moves, and we do not attribute it this cut.

In real terms the story is the same with slightly smaller numbers. Commissions were up 30.4% nominal and 26.1% in real 2026-06 dollars, using the desk-attached FRED CPIAUCSL series (base 2026-06 = 332.568, fetched 2026-09-17 ET). At the base quarter, real equals nominal by construction.

Activity: accounts and DARTs scaled together

DARTs per account was 0.930 in Q2’26 versus 0.919 a year earlier — activity per account roughly stable while the franchise scaled. DARTs grew 35.8% and accounts 34.1%; the two lines have moved together since the dense series began in 2023. One thing we refuse to do here: trading days per quarter are not disclosed, so there is no commissions-per-DART-day figure. The dollar companion to DART activity is the issuer's $2.64 per cleared order, full stop.

Scale per account tells the same steady story in dollars. Average customer equity was $179,421 per account in Q2’26, up from $156,310 when the dense window opened in early 2023. The second line is the same series in real 2026-06 CPIAUCSL dollars — a CPI normalization, not a beta attribution, and never a Pro/Lite or account-size cohort.

What carried the print

Of the +$157M year-over-year commissions increase in Q2’26, account growth contributed +$176M and per-account intensity −$19M — shares of roughly 1.12 and −0.12 of the change. On the 2024-onward window (eight quarters), the median split is about 1.16 from accounts and −0.16 from intensity. This is an exact identity — commissions equal accounts times commissions-per-account — not a causal model. But it answers the question cleanly: scale carried the print, and softer per-account take was a modest drag.

What co-moves with commissions

Both candidates co-move tightly with commissions. On the dense 2023-onward window, DARTs correlate slightly more tightly with commission levels (0.998 versus 0.991 for accounts, n=11); on YoY growth the two are roughly tied (accounts 0.881, DARTs 0.870); on QoQ growth DARTs edge it (0.872 versus 0.831). Meanwhile the dollar decomposition says account growth accounts for most of the year-over-year change. Our honest read: a larger, slightly less intense-per-unit franchise — not a broken toll. Correlation and decomposition are analysis, not proof of causation.

What we cannot see

  • Commission by geography — null. The geo P&L and the ASC 606 location revenue are not commissions. We use consolidated commissions and clearly labeled net-revenue proxies, and never call them geo commissions.
  • Account-size and Pro vs Lite cohorts — null. Average equity per account, DARTs per account, CPC, and the decomposition above are proxies, not invented cohorts.
  • API attach — gap. No issuer telemetry; the API moat stays qualitative.
  • Trading days — gap. Not disclosed; never invented.
  • NII — archive-only. Net interest income, NIM, and balances are inventoried but not in the analytics tables this cut. Noted, not charted, and not promoted into the fee-toll story.

Globality context, with the label intact: international was about 32% of management geo net revenues in Q2’26. That is a globality proxy — supportive context for the third pillar, not a fee-toll geo split.

Method & definitional notes
  • Nominal USD unless a series is explicitly labeled real. Real series use the desk-attached FRED CPIAUCSL deflator (base 2026-06 = 332.568, fetched 2026-09-17 ET; latest obs 2026-08-01 = 334.131). Nominal source values are unchanged.
  • House intensity SoT is the issuer's commission per cleared commissionable order (CPC). Trading days are not disclosed in the analytics SoT — no commissions/(DARTs × days), no $/DART-day.
  • Annualized fee yield is the quarterly ratio × 4 (simple), never TTM; the quarterly ratio is the primary series.
  • The accounts-vs-intensity decomposition is an exact identity (ΔC = I(t−4)·ΔA + A(t)·ΔI) and the correlations are co-movement reads — ANALYSIS, not causation.
  • Commission-by-geography is NULL: geo_pnl and ASC 606 location revenue are labeled proxies, never geo commissions.
  • Account-size and Pro/Lite cohorts are NULL: average equity/account, DARTs/account, CPC, and the decomposition are labeled proxies, not invented cohorts.
  • API attach remains a GAP (api-moat pack). NII / market-making are archive-only and are not charted in this dig.
  • PE is a sit-next-to footnote from the key-metrics pack (pe_ttm 34.67, price_asof 86.745 @ 2026-09-16; FY1 33.52, FY2 28.46 on 2026-W37) — no PE chart is rebuilt here and there is no dual-axis PE + price.
  • Derived rows require both numerator and denominator non-null; missing prints stay empty rather than backfilled.
